source: docs/cumbria-d1/published-network.json (Nico oracle-clash-report / Luke D1 pack, 1 Sep 2026)
notes: National Rail (Darwin/OpenLDBWS) is structurally catalogued here but blocked at the account level — DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN not set. Same blocker as every other UK region packed so far.

One tier-1 hub lock (Carlisle, CAR) plus two tier-2 secondary hubs (Oxenholme Lake District, OXN; Barrow-in-Furness, BIF) — each a genuine two-line junction, not co-equal with Carlisle. Penrith (PNR) is a major WCML station but not a junction, so it stays regional, not promoted to hub. See docs/cumbria-d1/direction-model-memo.md.

CRS codes live-verified against Darwin 5 Sep 2026 (see docs/jim-brief-uk-crs-sweep-2.md) — Oxenholme Lake District (OXO->OXN), Penrith (PEN->PNR), Windermere (WND->WDM), Kendal (KND->KEN), and Settle (SLF->SET) were all corrected from their originally-catalogued codes, which Darwin either rejected or resolved to unrelated stations elsewhere in Great Britain.

No doNotGroup case anywhere in this catalog — every junction (Carlisle, Oxenholme, Barrow-in-Furness) is a single physical station, unlike Liverpool City Region's Lime Street or Greater Manchester's Piccadilly/Piccadilly Gardens.

Caledonian Sleeper carries board-eligibility verdict out-reservation (compulsory berth booking) and is EXCLUDED from the board at Carlisle only — the sole Cumbrian station it calls. Northern Trains, TransPennine Express, Avanti West Coast all verdict 'in' at every station they call. CrossCountry's Cumbrian calling pattern is unconfirmed and not added to any station's operator list. See lib/providers/cumbria.js.

Only 7 of the report's claimed 48 Cumbrian stations are catalogued (Carlisle, Penrith, Oxenholme Lake District, Windermere, Kendal, Barrow-in-Furness, Settle) — the remaining ~41 are a recorded D2 gap, not invented. See docs/cumbria-d1/jim-handoff.md open item 2.

Regional boundaries checked against already-merged adjacent packs: Rest of Scotland does not claim Lockerbie or anything south of Perth/Inverness/Aberdeen/Dundee; Greater Manchester does not claim Preston, Wigan, or Settle. No live overlap found today.
No 'lines' array — no printed National Rail route/line map exists for Darwin, same structural fact as every National Rail-only region packed so far. Flat station list only.
Coordinates: NaPTAN RailReferences (CRS->coords) pulled 2026-09-07; 7/7 rail stations geocoded; no exceptions

stops.name: Carlisle
stops.class: hub lock — tier 1. 8 platforms. Junction of West Coast Main Line, Settle-Carlisle Line, Tyne Valley Line, Cumbrian Coast Line (four lines directly; a fifth, Lakes Line, reachable via Oxenholme). Northern Trains, Avanti West Coast, TransPennine Express all 'in'; Caledonian Sleeper 'out-reservation', excluded from board.

stops.name: Oxenholme Lake District
stops.class: hub lock — tier 2. West Coast Main Line junction with branch point to Lakes Line (Kendal, Windermere). Northern Trains, Avanti West Coast, TransPennine Express all 'in'.

stops.name: Barrow-in-Furness
stops.class: hub lock — tier 2. 3 platforms. Junction of Furness Line and Cumbrian Coast Line. Northern Trains only, 'in'.

stops.name: Penrith
stops.class: regional major station (not a junction — not promoted to tier-2 hub). West Coast Main Line, ~17 miles south of Carlisle. Northern Trains, Avanti West Coast, TransPennine Express all 'in'.

stops.name: Windermere
stops.class: Lakes Line branch terminus (Oxenholme -> Kendal -> Windermere). Northern Trains only, 'in'.

stops.name: Kendal
stops.class: Lakes Line, between Oxenholme and Windermere. Northern Trains only, 'in'.

stops.name: Settle
stops.class: Settle-Carlisle Line, ~48 miles south of Carlisle — southern boundary of Cumbria on this line (route continues south to Hellifield, outside Cumbria scope). Northern Trains only, 'in'.
